🚨🇲🇽 IN MEXICO, WELFARE IS NO LONGER A FAVOR TRADED FOR VOTES

"Social programs no longer depend on the vote." Sheinbaum said it handing Mujeres Bienestar pensions to women aged 60–64 in Tuxtla Chico, Chiapas — marking the break from the neoliberal era when welfare was a favor doled out at the ballot box. Under the 4T, pensions and scholarships are written into the Constitution. Rights, not handouts.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICAN EXPORTS JUMP 25.4% IN MAY — TRADE SURPLUS HOLDS THROUGH THE TARIFF WAR

INEGI reported Mexican exports hit $69.5 billion in May, up 25.4% year-on-year — non-oil exports up 25.6%, manufactured goods up 25.1% to nearly $63 billion. The trade balance stayed in surplus at $2.26 billion, and the five-month surplus reached $5.77 billion — versus just $918 million in the same period last year.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO REQUESTED 269 EXTRADITIONS FROM THE US SINCE 2018 — IT HAS RECEIVED ZERO

Between January 2018 and May 2026, Mexico filed 269 extradition requests with the United States — for organized crime, ex-governors' corruption, the Ayotzinapa case. Washington has returned exactly none. "¿Cuántos han sido devueltos a México? Ninguno," Sheinbaum said — 36 requests rejected, 233 still pending, among them ex-Tamaulipas governor Cabeza de Vaca.

🏳️‍⚧️🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM ON TRANS RIGHTS: STATE GOVERNMENTS MUST DO THEIR PART

As trans activists enter an eighth day of protest outside the Interior Ministry, Sheinbaum backed their demands and pointed to where much of the work lives: "Los registros civiles dependen de los estados" — civil registries, gender-identity recognition and birth-certificate changes are state matters. Their demands include specialized medical care, hormone therapy and a National Trans Law; housing, she said, should come through universal programs like Vivienda para el Bienestar, not segregated schemes.

🚨🇲🇽 US OFFICIAL CLAIMS CARTELS CONTROL "EVERY CENTIMETER" OF THE BORDER — SHEINBAUM: BUILD BRIDGES, NOT WALLS

US official Markwayne Mullin claimed "not a single centimeter of the border" escapes cartel control. Sheinbaum's reply: if Mexico weren't doing its work, how would fentanyl seizures at the US border be falling? Trump himself cited a 66% drop; the latest figure is nearly 74%. She called it what it is — Mexico turned into a prop for November's US midterms — and said what's needed are "more bridges, not walls."

🇲🇽⚽ MEXICO CITY SHUTS DOWN FOR EL TRI — CLASSES OFF, GOVERNMENT ON HOME OFFICE JUNE 30

By presidential decree published in the DOF, every school in Mexico City closes and the entire federal public service shifts to home office on June 30 — the day El Tri plays at the Estadio Azteca in the World Cup. It's the fourth such decree of the tournament, meant to ease mobility and road safety across the capital's south as Mexico hosts the world.

🇲🇽🌎 COLOMBIA'S INCOMING FAR-RIGHT PRESIDENT DECLARES MEXICAN CARTELS A "MILITARY TARGET" — SHEINBAUM: HANDLE YOUR OWN PART

Colombia's incoming far-right president Abelardo de la Espriella declared Mexican cartels a "military objective." Sheinbaum didn't flinch: "Que Colombia se encargue de su parte y nosotros de la nuestra" — let each country handle its own. She noted the two nations' armed forces already coordinate and exchange information, and that political differences between governments shouldn't be dragged into security theater.

🇲🇽🎨 A new national museum with no director — run by the artisans themselves. "This museum has no director; it is run by a council that makes decisions together with artisans and specialist craftspeople." — Claudia Curiel, Culture Secretary, on the Textile Museum The Museo Textil, dedicated to indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples, opened beside the Templo Mayor: twelve halls, interactive spaces and workshops. Museum and archaeological-site attendance rose 18% during the Social World Cup.
